clue.text: Setter's favourite American drive

parts.note: the setter speaking of himself: 'I am', shortened
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet
standard abbreviation for the United States

explanation.surface: A setter recalls a much-loved road trip across the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetus is the driving force or momentum behind something, a noun synonym of drive.

clue.text: Popular protocol for brief

parts.note: fashionable, 'in'
form means correct procedure or etiquette

explanation.surface: A short summary of an accepted procedure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' looks like an adjective but is the verb, to give instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: To brief someone is to give them information, a verb synonym of inform.

clue.text: Promise place on border

parts.note: abbreviation for place, as on maps
a ledge is a narrow edge or border

explanation.surface: A vow to locate something at the frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: A pledge is a solemn promise or undertaking, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Here today gone tomorrow politician under terrible strain

indicators.note: in a down clue under puts the politician below the other piece
terrible suggests something in a bad state, so the letters of the next word are disordered

parts.note: taken as written
a Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A short-lived politician cracks under heavy pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: Transitory means lasting only briefly, which the phrase here today, gone tomorrow describes idiomatically.

clue.text: Great American revolutionary period cut by half

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the word for American is read backwards

parts.note: abbreviation for the United States

indicators.note: cut by half means only half of the word for period is kept

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A splendid era of the American Revolution was cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: Super is an informal adjective meaning excellent or wonderful, the same as great.

clue.text: Plymouth Brethren originally loaded with cargo of different plant

indicators.note: a vehicle loaded with cargo carries it inside, so one piece is held within the other
originally points to how each word begins, so only the opening letters of the named group are kept

parts.note: the initials of this Christian movement
other means different

explanation.surface: A religious group sails off carrying a ship's hold full of some unfamiliar plant.
explanation.walkthrough: OTHER sits between P and B to make POT HERB.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot herb is any plant grown for its leaves to use in cooking, such as parsley or sorrel.

clue.text: Projects of organised tour taken by prim types

indicators.note: taken by means held inside the word that follows

parts.note: prudes are prim, easily shocked people

indicators.note: something organised has been arranged, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: the word as printed, but the parse has room for only three of its letters, as its U is surplus: the setter's slip

explanation.surface: A prim group signs up for a package holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is flawed as printed: four rearranged letters inside a six-letter word would make ten, but the answer has nine, so one U must do double duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Protrudes, a verb, means sticks out, which is what projects means as a verb.

clue.text: Dog brush

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a fox's bushy ... is called its brush

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a grooming tool for a pet, but 'Dog' is a verb and 'brush' is a fox's tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Tail means to shadow someone, and a fox's tail is known in hunting as its brush.

clue.text: How boxers may see confrontation — or agreement?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: facing each other directly, as boxers do
second meaning: to see things the same way

explanation.surface: Fighters stare each other down, yet perhaps they agree.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase covers both a face-off and, in 'see ___', complete agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Facing off head to head is a confrontation, while the idiom see eye to eye means being in accord.

clue.text: Support for building may be very French, beset by objections

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded on all sides, so one piece lies inside the other

parts.note: buts are objections, as in no ifs or buts
the French word for very

explanation.surface: A French building project draws plenty of objections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very French' means the French word for very, not something very French in style.
explanation.definitionFit: A buttress is a projecting structure of masonry that supports a wall, so it braces a building.

clue.text: Revolutionary part of prayer for a deity

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns things round, so the run is read right to left
part of says the letters come from a run inside the following words

parts.note: the letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A rebel's segment of a prayer is addressed to some god.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'prAYER For' backwards to find the goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: Freya is the Norse goddess of love and fertility, so she is one example of a deity.

clue.text: Supply books, exercising caution

parts.note: to provide is to supply
New Testament, a collection of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A careful buyer stocks up on books.
explanation.definitionFit: A provident person is prudent, planning ahead for future needs, which is an adjective sense matching careful foresight.

clue.text: People who keep records of doctors in hospital

definitions.meaning: first meaning: officials recording births, marriages and deaths
second meaning: in Britain, a grade of hospital doctor below consultant

explanation.surface: Clerks keep the files on hospital doctors.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one phrase, records of doctors, but splits after 'records'. In British hospitals a registrar is a senior trainee doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: The same plural noun names both civil record-keeping officials and a rank of hospital physician in Britain.

clue.text: Fly in pain, by all accounts

indicators.note: accounts are things people say, so the word is judged by its spoken sound

parts.note: sore means hurting, in pain

explanation.surface: Someone apparently travels by air while suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: To soar is to fly high in the air, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Welcome resignation

definitions.meaning: second meaning: submission to what cannot be changed

explanation.walkthrough: 'Resignation' suggests quitting a job, but here it means being resigned to something.
explanation.definitionFit: Acceptance can mean being received warmly, and also calmly submitting to fate, both noun senses.

clue.text: Fliers once caught in old tapestry after restoration

indicators.note: in places one element among the letters of the phrase that follows
restoring a damaged piece reworks it, so the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
cricket scoring abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Restorers find winged creatures woven into an antique tapestry.
explanation.definitionFit: Pterodactyls were flying reptiles of the dinosaur age, extinct long ago, hence fliers of former times.

clue.text: Morally good having forged rough ties

indicators.note: forged means hammered into a new form, so the letters are remade in another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An upright person is caught with crude, crooked connections.
explanation.definitionFit: Righteous describes someone acting justly and virtuously, an adjective synonym of morally good.

clue.text: Timetable from school — avoid retrospective

parts.note: standard abbreviation for school

indicators.note: retrospective means looking back, so the word for avoid runs backwards

parts.note: to elude is to avoid or escape

explanation.surface: A school's timetable lets pupils dodge a backward-looking review.
explanation.definitionFit: A schedule is a plan listing times of events, which is what a timetable is.

clue.text: Man's man?

parts.note: surface reading: a man's manservant or valet
setter's reading: Man is the Isle of Man, so a man of Man is someone living there

explanation.walkthrough: The capitalised 'Man' is hidden by the start of the clue; the Isle of Man is a self-governing island between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone native to the Isle of Man is an inhabitant of an island, so a man of Man is such a resident.

clue.text: When in church notice where money may be put

indicators.note: in places the first word inside the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: standard abbreviation for church
as can mean when, as in 'as he left'
to register something is to notice it

explanation.surface: A churchgoer spots the collection plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When' can be replaced by 'as', as in 'as he left'; the definition is a whole phrase at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A cash register is the till in a shop, the machine into which payments are placed.

clue.text: Refuse large beer with no head

indicators.note: with no head means the first letter of the beer is cut off

parts.note: abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels
bitter is a British style of beer

explanation.surface: Someone turns down a big pint that has gone flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb but is the noun, rubbish. Bitter is a hoppy British ale.
explanation.definitionFit: Litter is rubbish dropped about, the same as refuse in its noun sense.

clue.text: Was aware of poles getting in the way of top player

indicators.note: getting in the way of means intruding into the next word, so those letters go inside it

parts.note: a seed is a top-ranked player in a tournament
the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Someone noticed the poles obstructing the star tennis player.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis and other knockout tournaments the top-ranked entrants are seeded to keep them apart early on.
explanation.definitionFit: To sense something is to perceive or be conscious of it, so sensed is a past-tense equivalent.

clue.text: Style found in Michelangelo?

indicators.note: found in says the answer is lying inside the name that follows

parts.note: a run of letters inside the painter's name

explanation.surface: An art critic praises the flair of the great Renaissance artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Elan means flair, verve or panache, which is stylishness, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Fly — like a London cabby perhaps

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in British slang, fly means sharp and knowing
second meaning, read literally: wise about streets, as a cab driver who knows every road

explanation.surface: An insect is compared to a taxi driver in London.
explanation.walkthrough: London black-cab drivers must pass 'the Knowledge', learning every street in the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Streetwise means shrewd in the ways of urban life, which is what the slang adjective fly means.

clue.text: Bonus ball

definitions.meaning: second meaning: in cricket, a wide or no-ball counts as a run not scored by the batsman

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like the Lottery's bonus ball; in cricket, runs from wides and no-balls are called extras.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra is an additional item, and in cricket a wide or no-ball delivery yields an extra run.

clue.text: Language repressed regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter is kept

parts.note: the even-placed letters

explanation.surface: A tongue that has been persistently held down.
explanation.definitionFit: Erse is an old name for the Gaelic tongue of Scotland or Ireland, so it is one particular language.

clue.text: Where an arch must be in the way?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the arch of a foot is on its underside
second meaning: obstructing, getting under one's feet

explanation.surface: An architect asks where a bridge's arch has to be placed if it is not to obstruct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arch' suggests building, but it is the arch of the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Something underfoot is beneath your feet and so obstructive, and the foot's arch is literally at its base.

clue.text: Observes attack being repelled

indicators.note: an attack that is repelled is driven back, so the phrase runs backwards

parts.note: to set on someone is to attack them

explanation.surface: A watcher reports an assault being driven off.
explanation.definitionFit: To note something is to observe or remark it, matching the present-tense verb.

clue.text: Students with no end of useful cash jobs

indicators.note: with no signals a letter being taken out of the word for students

parts.note: learners are students

indicators.note: 'end of' keeps only the last letter of 'useful'

parts.note: the final letter of useful

explanation.surface: Students lacking useful skills take cash-in-hand work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End of' is a selector here, picking the last letter of 'useful'.
explanation.definitionFit: Earners are things that bring in money, so a nice little earner is a lucrative job.

clue.text: Said Bible was wrong

parts.note: the Authorised Version of the Bible
to err is to be wrong

explanation.surface: Someone claimed the scriptures were mistaken.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to state firmly, so averred is a past-tense equivalent of said.
